name: Feet-Elevated Ring Push-Up
description: A challenging combination of ring instability and decline body angle that shifts the loading emphasis toward the upper and clavicular portions of the pectoralis major. With feet elevated on a bench and hands in gymnastic rings, the athlete must simultaneously stabilize the unstable rings and generate pressing force, creating significant demands on the chest, anterior deltoid, and scapular stabilizers.

execution.starting_position: Set rings at approximately knee height. Place feet on a sturdy bench behind you, hands in rings below your shoulders. Body forms a decline plank position with arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure rings at a consistent height. The elevation of the feet relative to hand height determines the degree of decline. Set rings close together (shoulder width) for more chest emphasis.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the top position with arms extended, body forming a straight inclined plank from feet (elevated) to hands (rings below).
Step 2: Lower your chest toward the rings, allowing elbows to flare slightly while keeping rings stable.
Step 3: Descend until chest is level with or just below the rings.
Step 4: Press powerfully back to the starting position, squeezing the chest at the top.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on the press upward.
common_mistakes: Letting the rings wobble uncontrollably — build ring stability before adding feet elevation
Pike hips to reduce difficulty, breaking the straight line
Flaring elbows excessively causing shoulder impingement
safety_considerations: Establish proficiency with flat ring push-ups before elevating feet
Ensure the bench is stable and will not slide when feet are placed on it
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from arms extended to chest at ring level. Turn rings out slightly at top position (rings turn out or RTO) to increase pectoral contraction.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-1-1-1 (3s descent, 1s pause at bottom, 1s press, 1s RTO hold)
coaching_cues: Turn the rings out at the top — externally rotate wrists
Keep the body in one rigid plank — no sagging or piking
